scope: app/ and tests/ only (CHG-003 / R17, CHG-004 / R18)
tests_run: python -m pytest tests/unit/test_auth.py tests/unit/test_auth_service.py tests/unit/test_dependencies.py tests/unit/test_notifications.py -q -> 72 passed, exit 0

findings.message: The keep-alive loop only exits on WebSocketDisconnect, but it never awaits websocket.receive(), which is the only place Starlette raises that exception. Under uvicorn 0.29 [standard] a real client disconnect surfaces from the send side (websockets ConnectionClosed), which suppress(WebSocketDisconnect) does not catch, so every disconnect escapes the handler and uvicorn logs an 'Exception in ASGI application' traceback. The new finally block still unregisters the socket, so the registry stays correct; the impact is log noise plus an untested exit path. The test proves it only because _disconnect_after_one_ping monkeypatches asyncio.sleep to raise WebSocketDisconnect, which cannot happen in production.
findings.fix: Widen the suppressed exception set on the loop (e.g. suppress(WebSocketDisconnect, ConnectionError, RuntimeError)) or drive the loop with a receive() task so the disconnect arrives as WebSocketDisconnect, and add one test that raises the send-side error instead of a synthetic asyncio.sleep failure.

findings.message: `code: str` is an unannotated scalar on a POST route, so FastAPI binds it as a query parameter. The one-time TOTP code therefore travels in the request line and lands in nginx/uvicorn access logs, proxy logs and browser history. The diff rewrote this signature (removing user_id) and left `code` where it was. CHG-003 records this as a deferred follow-up, so it does not block, but it is the last remaining transport weakness on the path this story hardens.
findings.fix: Move `code` into a Pydantic request body model (e.g. `body: TotpVerifyRequest`) in a follow-up; the cookie-based user derivation already lands, so this is a one-line signature change plus the schema.

findings.message: push_to_user logs a failed send but never unregisters the dead socket, so a socket whose ping loop has not yet terminated stays in _connections and re-logs notifications.ws_push_failed on every subsequent push (log amplification, unbounded registry growth for long-lived processes). AC5 only requires the log line, so this is an observation rather than a story gap.
findings.fix: Call _unregister(user_id, ws) in the except branch after logging.

findings.message: Asymmetry introduced by the diff: get_current_user now delegates claim extraction to session_user_id(), while get_current_admin still inlines decode_access_token() + payload.get('admin_sub') + the new `'purpose' in payload` guard. The purpose rule now lives in two places, so a future third token purpose must be remembered twice.
findings.fix: Add an admin_user_id(token) helper next to session_user_id() in app/services/auth_service.py and have get_current_admin call it.

findings.message: The WebSocket authorises on the signed token alone, so unlike get_current_user it never re-checks that the user still exists, is_active, and has totp_verified. A deactivated user keeps receiving live pushes for the remaining life of the 8-hour cookie. CHG-004 declares this explicitly out of scope, so it is recorded, not charged against the diff.
findings.fix: None required for this story. If it is picked up later, resolve the User row before accept() the same way get_current_user does.

findings.message: The pending cookie name is expressed twice: the PENDING_2FA_COOKIE constant on the write side and the bare parameter name `pending_2fa` on the read side. Renaming the constant would silently stop the endpoint from reading the cookie it sets.
findings.fix: Bind the read through the constant: `pending_2fa: Optional[str] = Cookie(default=None, alias=PENDING_2FA_COOKIE)`.

findings.message: The pending_2fa cookie is cleared only on the success path. After a 400 (bad code), an abandoned enrolment, or logout it stays in the browser until its 10-minute Max-Age elapses. Bounded by the TTL and by the totp_verified single-use check, so the exposure is small.
findings.fix: No change needed; if tightened later, delete the cookie on the 400 branch too.

findings.message: The pending_2fa cookie is Secure, so the TOTP enrolment flow cannot complete over plain http (e.g. the docker compose app on http://localhost:8000). This matches the existing access_token cookie, which is already Secure, so it is consistent rather than a regression - noting it because it makes local manual testing of the new flow require TLS.
findings.fix: None. Exercise the flow through the TLS-terminating nginx service or via the unit tests.

findings.message: callback() is still ~82 lines (provider dispatch + user creation + session issue), over the 30-line project limit. Pre-existing and grandfathered; the diff moved 11 lines out of it into _totp_setup_response, so the ratchet moved the right way. Recorded as context only.
findings.fix: None in this change. A later refactor could extract the per-provider userinfo parsing into a _userinfo(provider, client, token) helper.

verified_correct: AC1: pending cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Lax/Max-Age=600/Path=/api/auth/totp, JWT carries sub + purpose=totp_setup with exp-iat == 600, and no access_token is set on that branch.
Cookie path /api/auth/totp path-matches /api/auth/totp/verify per RFC 6265 5.1.4 and does not match a sibling like /api/auth/totpfoo.

AC2/AC3: verify derives the user only from the cookie; missing, expired, bad-signature, wrong-purpose, subject-less and plain-session tokens all 401 before any DB query (asserted via db.queries == 0).
AC4: totp_verified commit, access_token issue, pending cookie cleared on the same path, unchanged response body.
AC6/AC8: session_user_id rejects any token with a purpose claim; get_current_admin rejects purpose-bound tokens; a pending token is spent once its user is totp_verified.

No other call site decodes access tokens - decode_access_token has exactly three callers (dependencies.py, auth_service.py), so there is no third path where a purpose-bound token would still pass as a session.

R18: close(1008) happens before accept() and before registration for missing/garbage/expired/pending-2fa/other-user tokens; the finally + _unregister pair fixes the old KeyError/ValueError cleanup and preserves the user's other sockets.
Control flow of the OAuth callback is unchanged by the _totp_setup_response extraction; no schema provisioning or audit event was skipped or duplicated.
No test file or assertion was deleted (35 deletions, all in app/); the branch adds 754 lines of tests across 4 files and all 72 pass.
